subtopic: Deciding whether to report a cheating friend
subtype: Approach: sleeping on it before acting [Thinking]
passage:
Dear Zubin bhai,
You said never to decide anything when I'm this angry, so I'm writing to say I listened. Yesterday in the physics test I saw my friend Sameer copying from under his desk. I almost stormed to Sir's table right then. My hands were shaking and my head was full of speeches. Instead I went home, ate dinner and did nothing. I slept badly, but by morning the anger had shrunk. I realised I would have been shouting, and a rushed complaint might have sounded more like revenge than fairness. So here's my plan: talk to Sameer privately at lunch and ask him to tell Sir himself, and if nothing changes by next week, I'll tell Sir myself. Thank you for the rule.
Your cousin,
Akash

qa.q: When will Akash tell Sir if nothing changes?
qa.a: Akash will tell Sir if nothing changes by next week.

qa.q: How did Akash feel right after seeing Sameer copy?
qa.a: Akash felt angry, with shaking hands and a head full of speeches.

qa.q: What could Akash do if Sameer refuses to talk?
qa.a: Akash could take it to the teacher calmly, as planned, since one fair chance has already been given.

qa.q: How might Sameer feel when Akash talks to him privately?
qa.a: Sameer may feel surprised and nervous, but a quiet talk lets Sameer respond without being shamed in front of the class.

grounding: A student holds back for a night, cools down and decides on a private conversation followed by a teacher if nothing changes, instead of a rushed angry act.
